data.name: Ataur
data.gender_notes: Ataur is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ataur is a Sanskrit name derived from the word ‘asva’, meaning horse or cattle. The name Ataur is believed to be the lord of cattle and is often used as a name for a protector or a provider. In Hindu mythology, Ataur is associated with the god Indra, who is the god of rain, thunder, and lightning. As a protector and provider, Indra is believed to look after the cattle and the agricultural produce.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents strength and protection in agriculture and livestock
data.etymology: Ataur belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the cattle.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ataur total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ataur holds cultural significance in Hindu traditions as it is associated with the god Indra, who is considered as the lord of the cattle and known as the giver of rain and prosperity in agriculture. The name carries the divine blessings of abundance and wealth, particularly for those working in the agricultural sector.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Ataur lies in its connection to the Hindu god Indra, who is the embodiment of power, strength, and protection. A name like Ataur holds deep spiritual significance for individuals who seek to invoke the blessings of this powerful deity, particularly those who are seeking protection, prosperity, and blessings for their agricultural produce and livestock.
